reader.decision: Approve raising both limits to 200 MB now (nginx on /api/files only, Flask MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH), with presigned upload planned after 9 November.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows the 10m caps in nginx and Flask are the cause, the logs confirm 413s at nginx, and the two-line change meets Friday without a frontend release. The checked disk, timeout and scope figures show the cost is acceptable.

reconstruction.problem: Halvorsen Marine's CAD drawings (60-180 MB) fail to upload because nginx client_max_body_size is 10m server-wide and Flask MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is 10 MiB. nginx returns 413 on Content-Length before reading the body (log entries at 09:14 and 09:31 on 2026-10-27).
reconstruction.what_breaks: Every drawing of 60-180 MB fails with 413, and the yard review on Monday 2 November is at risk. Raising only nginx would not help, because Flask would then return 413 at its own limit.
reconstruction.fix: Add an exact-match location = /api/files in deploy/nginx/pinewood.conf with client_max_body_size 200m and the same proxy_pass and headers, keeping 10m elsewhere. Change MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH in app/settings.py to 200 * 1024 * 1024. Later, move to direct-to-bucket upload via presign_post, which needs a new endpoint and a web client change.
reconstruction.cost: nginx disk-buffers each upload (about 72 s for 180 MB at 2.5 MB/s, with no gunicorn worker held). Each upload holds one of the 4 sync workers for about 3 s. Any account can send 200 MB to /api/files, and a per-account limit needs separate work. The presigned alternative needs frontend work that cannot happen before 9 November.

reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve raising both limits to 200 MB now, with the presigned upload planned for after 9 November.
